messages:
opsbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated 5xx rates observed from eu-west-1 edge tier; automatic fallback attempted to model variant `redwood-v1-q4` but ~12% of requests got routed to lower-tier cold pool. Pager to oncall.
Maya G: I’m on it. grabbing logs and will triage routing decisions.
Liam R: I can cover mitigation — ready to roll traffic to controlled canary if needed.
Anika S: linking trace aggregator: https://logs.redwood.internal/trace/ea1f2c — lots of retries around 14:32:10 UTC
Devon P: question — did the fallback model choose a smaller-capacity stack? I saw some `capacity_tier` mismatches earlier.
Maya G: quick snapshot of what opsbot shows:
```
incident_id: INC-2026-2309876543
start: 2026-03-15T14:32:03Z
symptom: 5xx spike on eu-west-1, P99 latency +500ms
auto_fallback_target: redwood-v1-q4
fallback_attempts: 3
failed_routes: ~450
```

Maya G: initial timeline:
- 14:32:02Z: region overload telemetry crosses threshold
- 14:32:03Z: opsbot issues automatic fallback policy (policy v2.1)
- 14:32:04Z: routing-engine computes candidate pool (should prefer dedicated hot pool)
- 14:32:05Z: subset of traffic routed to cold pool in eu-west-3 (unexpected)
- 14:33:10Z: spike of 502/504 responses detected
- 14:34:00Z: oncall paged

Liam R: pasted small log excerpt — note the tiebreak calc:
```
[14:32:04Z] route_decision: selected_pool=eu-west-3-cold weight_score=0.0012
[14:32:04Z] policy_eval: prefer_hot_pool=true but fallback_cost_estimate=high
[14:32:04Z] pool_health: eu-west-1-hot ok, eu-west-3-cold degraded
```

Liam R: that weight_score math looks off — 0.0012 should not beat hot pool. maybe wrong normalizer.
Anika S: hypothesis A: normalization bug in the weight calc after we added jitter to prefer region-local pools.
Anika S: hypothesis B: pool health aggregation latency — health was stale and showed hot pool as unhealthy for a brief window.
Devon P: hypothesis C: model compatibility filter mismatched quantized variant and flagged hot pool as incompatible, forcing a lower-weight cold fallback.
Maya G: collecting KV cache telemetry and model-compat logs now — will paste relevant lines.
Maya G: KV cache snippet:
```
[14:32:03Z] kvcache.check: model=redwood-v1-q4 compatible=true
[14:32:03Z] kvcache.check: pool=eu-west-1-hot stale=false
[14:32:04Z] kvcache.check: pool=eu-west-3-cold compatible=true
```

Rachel K: i’m pulling routing-engine profiler. grabbing stack traces around 14:32:04.
Rachel K: profiler note: normalization loop used `total_capacity` value that was temporarily zero for eu-west-1-hot due to a reporting lag.
Liam R: that would explain weight inversion. if total_capacity=0 then any nonzero weight from cold pool wins.
Maya G: confirmed: metrics ingestion shows a 6s gap for eu-west-1-hot capacity counter due to metric-aggregator restart (deploy).
Devon P: did deploy touch the region metrics shard? which change triggered aggregator restart?
Rachel K: deploys around 14:31:58 to monitoring-agent; rolling restarts caused a brief scrape failure.
Anika S: mitigation proposal (live):
- suspend automatic fallback for 2m in eu-west until metrics stabilize :gear:
- add explicit fallback target override to `eu-global-canary` for critical customers :white_check_mark:

Liam R: executing emergency override: `routing-cli set-policy override-fallback eu-global-canary --duration=2m`
Maya G: override applied at 14:33:15Z. watching error rate.
opsbot: action taken: override applied by Liam R.
Maya G: after override, 5xxs drop back toward baseline by 14:34:10Z, P99 latency normalizing.
Devon P: customer impact check — can we enumerate impacted customers? opsbot link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/impacted/INC-2026-2309876543
Maya G: initial list from access logs: two high-traffic tenants saw degraded responses for ~45s (partial success for some sessions). details in the link.
Anika S: we should capture hypothesis notes in-thread for RCA:
- H1: metric-aggregator restart caused 0 capacity reading -> weight normalizer zero-division or floor behaviour -> routes chosen incorrectly.
- H2: model-compat filter flagged hot pool due to transient config propagation -> pool excluded.
- H3: tie-break jitter change increased sensitivity to tiny weight differences.

Rachel K: evidence ranking: H1 (strong) > H3 (medium) > H2 (weak). profiler + metric timestamps line up to H1.
Liam R: next steps (assigned):
- Maya G: gather full timeline + loglinks (in progress)
- Rachel K: confirm aggregator change and revert strategy if needed
- Devon P: audit model-compat filter propagation logs
- Anika S: write temporary guard in routing-engine to treat missing capacity as unknown rather than zero

Maya G: pasted timeline doc draft: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-2309876543/timeline (internal)
Maya G: log bundle uploaded: https://s3.redwood.internal/inc-2309876543/logs.tar.gz

Devon P: proposed immediate post-incident mitigation: ensure metric-aggregator deployes are staggered per-region and add a 30s grace window before using capacity counters in weight calc.
Anika S: agree. also add an alert if capacity reads zero for a healthy pool to avoid silent inversion.
Liam R: I'll schedule a quick follow-up call at 15:00 UTC for a live RCA sync and owners alignment.
Maya G: status update: incident resolved, override removed at 14:36:10Z, normal routing resumed. preparing a concise incident summary for customers.
opsbot: INCIDENT CLOSED (auto) at 14:36:15Z — severity downgraded to SEV-3.
Maya G: will post a short blameless timeline and action items to the incidents channel and link to the postmortem doc.
Anika S: notes to include in postmortem: root cause = temporary metric gap from aggregator restart -> bad weight normalization; mitigating changes: guard for zero readings, staggered deploys, canary override improvements.
Liam R: assigning follow-ups in ticketing system now. :spiral_notepad: 
Rachel K: thanks everyone — nice quick coordination.
Maya G: closing thread — will attach final RCA link when ready. :white_check_mark:
